S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  CRLA No.221 of 2020  With  CRMA/2282/2020 (Bail Application)
 Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Present Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, learned counsel for the appellant/applicant.
Present Mr. G.S. Sandhu, learned Government Advocate assisted by Mrs. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
2.

Present criminal appeal is preferred by the appellant/applicant against the judgment/order dated 27.02.2020 passed by learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, District Udham Singh Nagar, in Sessions Trial No.261 of 2012, whereby the appellant/applicant has been convicted under Sections 304B, 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and has been sentenced to undergo ten years, two years and one year rigorous imprisonment respectively along with total fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine he is directed to undergo further one month additional imprisonment.
3. Heard on the Bail Application (CRMA/2282/2020).
4.

entities.text: 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, District Udham Singh Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for the appellant/applicant undertakes to deposit the fine amount.

5. Counsel for the appellant/applicant would submit that in compliance of the order dated 07.11.2023 passed by this Court, the State has filed a short counter affidavit stating therein that on 25.01.2024 the appellant/applicant has already served the sentence of for the period of six years and eight days, therefore, he is entitled to bail as per Section 436A of the Cr.P.C. as he has already undergone half of the period of sentence awarded to him.

He would further submit that the role assigned to the appellant/applicant in the commission of the offence, as per the judgment, is not more than to the role assigned to the other co-convicts, who have already been granted bail; that, the final disposal of the appeal may take considerable time,
CRLA/221/2020 on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198593403/
1 therefore, the appellant/applicant should be released on bail during the pendency of the present case.
6.

Per contra, State counsel opposed the bail of the appellant/applicant only on the ground that Section 436A Cr.P.C. the words used are "can be"
meaning thereby that an accused under an offence is entitled to be released having undergone detention of one-half of the maximum period of imprisonment specified for that offence but in the instant case the appellant/applicant has been convicted under Section 304-B of I.P.C., under which, the maximum punishment prescribed is life imprisonment, therefore, the benefit of Section 436A Cr.P.C. cannot be extended to the appellant/applicant.

7. In the considered view of this Court, this submission of the learned Government Advocate is misplaced because the words 'can be awarded' essentially refers to the situation when the trial is underway and when the conviction has already been secured by the prosecution and the sentence has been awarded, then the period of imprisonment awarded in the sentence shall be considered for the purposes of bail as per Section 436A of the Cr.P.C.
8.
In view of the above, without expressing any opinion about the merits of the appeal, the appellant/ applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail during the pendency of the present criminal appeal.

9. Let the appellant/ applicant be released on bail on furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the amount of 70,000/- each and personal bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.
10.
Bail application stands disposed of accordingly.

11. List this case on 04.06.2024 for final hearing.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)
